body:
[aida:product] #2026 done and pushed (9c38af7d83). BUG-1546 merged as fe62ee6e89. Starting #2027, which is the same defect class I just reproduced in my own test.

ONE OF THREE DONE. #2026 is reworked, rebased onto current main, pushed, MERGEABLE, and back with the reviewer. I am not merging it — independence, and merge is yours.

THE SEAM WENT THE WAY THE MEASUREMENT SAID. View type, `display_members()`, all three renderers call it, the human special case deleted rather than duplicated, JSON overriding the serde-emitted key with the same view. The loader option stayed out on the evidence: six mutate-then-write sites, five writing back through the same value.

VERIFICATION: fmt clean, full suite 5226 passed 0 failed exit 0 read before the push, and four mutations — revert TOON 1 red, remove the JSON override 1 red, persist the view 1 red, never produce the synthetic 2 red, restored 63 green. The third of those is the one that matters: it simulates the loader option and proves the safety test would catch it, so a future "simplification" back into the state fails loudly instead of corrupting drain state silently.

THE THING WORTH YOUR ATTENTION. My first TOON assertion passed with the TOON fix reverted. TOON emits `current` as a scalar, so a bare contains() on the document found the spec id whether or not the members table was fixed. The mutation caught it; nothing else would have. I have disclosed it to the reviewer rather than quietly correcting it.

That is the SEVENTH instance tonight of the same underlying error, and it is worth naming precisely because the surface keeps changing: a correct observation attached to a population or a scope it does not actually cover. Five were wrong denominators, one was the doc comment, and this one is an assertion whose scope was the whole document when the claim was about one table. The measurement is never the broken part. What breaks is the boundary I attach it to.

AND #2027 IS THE SAME CLASS, WHICH IS WHY I FLAG IT NOW. Its refusal reads: the journey test "independently searches each output for hard-coded substrings, so disagreement in row cardinality, target association, ordering, or extra collapsed rows can still pass. Parse/normalize both relationship sections and compare the resulting typed edges." That is exactly the defect I just committed and fixed inside #2026's test, one layer out. The remedy transfers directly, including `toon::parse_table`.

I am starting #2027 now unless you want it ordered differently. #2033 after, then I stop and report as ruled.

BUG-1546 auto-bumped to Completed on merge. BUG-1441 is still Done and I have left it there — the rework does not change that it is work finished on a branch awaiting merge.
subject: #2026 pushed at 9c38af7d83, BUG-1546 merged. Starting #2027 — same defect class (substring search vs parsed projection), seventh instance of the same boundary error
